review_type: Targeted narrative literature search; not a systematic review

references.label: Fuller et al., 2006
references.title: Consensus statement on injury definitions and data collection procedures in studies of football (soccer) injuries
references.claim: Standardized injury, recurrence and exposure definitions support interpretable comparisons.
references.limitation: A consensus does not verify compliance or medical accuracy of the Kaggle archive.

references.label: Bahr et al., 2020
references.title: International Olympic Committee consensus statement: methods for recording and reporting of epidemiological data on injury and illness in sport 2020 (including STROBE Extension for Sport Injury and Illness Surveillance (STROBE-SIIS))
references.relevance: Exposure, time loss, burden and transparent reporting
references.claim: Exposure and consequences must be recorded with definitions appropriate to the question.
references.limitation: Does not supply missing exposure or eligibility denominators.

references.label: Waldén et al., 2023
authors: Dina Christina Christa Janse van Rensburg
references.title: Football-specific extension of the IOC consensus statement: methods for recording and reporting of epidemiological data on injury and illness in sport 2020
references.relevance: Updated football injury and illness nomenclature
references.claim: Football surveillance benefits from consistent definitions, collection procedures and reporting.
references.limitation: Does not establish specific diagnoses from vague source labels.

references.label: Bahr, Clarsen and Ekstrand, 2018
references.title: Why we should focus on the burden of injuries and illnesses, not just their incidence
references.relevance: Joint interpretation of frequency and consequence
references.claim: Consequences should accompany event frequency when prioritizing health problems.
references.limitation: Conceptual guidance; not a validation study or a predictive model.

references.label: Hägglund et al., 2013
references.title: Injuries affect team performance negatively in professional football: an 11-year follow-up of the UEFA Champions League injury study
references.claim: Lower burden and higher match availability were associated with better team performance.
references.limitation: Observational association; does not establish causality or the same relation in this archive.

references.label: Ekstrand et al., 2023
references.title: Hamstring injury rates have increased during recent seasons and now constitute 24% of all injuries in men's professional football: the UEFA Elite Club Injury Study from 2001/02 to 2021/22
references.relevance: Hamstring frequency and burden over time
references.claim: The monitored cohort documented increasing hamstring injury and absence-day proportions over 21 seasons.
references.limitation: Its clinical categories and exposure-based trends are not directly comparable with raw Kaggle labels.

references.label: Krutsch et al., 2020
references.title: Injury Analysis in Professional Soccer by Means of Media Reports – Only Severe Injury Types Show High Validity
references.journal: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
references.relevance: Missing public records and diagnostic validity
references.claim: Media records included missing and incorrect injury information, with better agreement for some severe types.
references.limitation: Findings are source- and setting-specific, not a universal correction factor.

references.label: Hoenig et al., 2022
references.title: Analysis of more than 20,000 injuries in European professional football by using a citizen science-based approach: An opportunity for epidemiological research?
references.journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
references.claim: The public archive showed lower injury recording and a higher severe-injury proportion than comparator sources.
references.limitation: Does not independently establish the upstream provenance or accuracy of the current Kaggle version.

references.label: Aus der Fünten et al., 2023
references.title: Epidemiology of Football Injuries of the German Bundesliga: A Media-Based, Prospective Analysis over 7 Consecutive Seasons
references.claim: A defined multi-source protocol can support league-wide surveillance while retaining diagnosis limitations.
references.limitation: A downloaded event archive does not recreate its prospective collection and exposure procedures.

references.label: Ardern et al., 2016
references.title: 2016 Consensus statement on return to sport from the First World Congress in Sports Physical Therapy, Bern
references.relevance: Distinct return milestones and endpoint meaning
references.claim: Return to sport involves a progression and multifactorial shared decisions.
references.limitation: A recorded interval end does not establish medical clearance or return to performance.

references.label: Ekstrand, Hägglund and Waldén, 2011
references.title: Epidemiology of muscle injuries in professional football (soccer)
references.relevance: Muscle injury consequences and clinical reinjury
references.claim: Muscle injuries produced substantial absence and clinically defined reinjuries had longer absences than index injuries.
references.limitation: Repeated free-text labels do not reproduce clinical reinjury definitions.

references.label: Bengtsson et al., 2025
references.title: No major changes in injury incidence in European club football during the 2022/23 FIFA World Cup season: a subanalysis of the UEFA Elite Club Injury Study
references.claim: The study found no major overall change in incidence during the World Cup season versus its historical comparator, with setting-specific nuances.
references.limitation: Does not show that congestion is harmless in every setting or explain this archive's monthly counts.
